items.title: 68146_Russell Procope oral history interview
items.q: You did a lot of things with Langworth too, transcriptions. ... Oh, yes. We had a transcription date every month.

ctx.x: Yes. That's true. Yes. Then we had a sustaining program. We broadcast every Sunday around -- I think it was 12:00 or 1:00 o'clock on Sunday afternoon. And of course it required a lot of music, you know. Every Sunday was a different program. And the band wasn't -- wasn't very old then. I would say it was a year old, if that old. So everything was tense and, you know, and you had to be -- you had to give 150 percent every Sunday, and we didn't have much time to rehearse or anything like that. I think at that time…
You did a lot of things with Langworth too, transcriptions.

Oh, yes. We had a transcription date every month. We were working at the Onyx Club, we had a record date every month, we had this transcription every month, which for those days was as much as any group in our position, I'd say, you know, could have done. We had the commercial and the job at the Onyx Club and the transcription, a month. So it all -- and we were working real hard. We really worked hard.
